card.name: Opening verbs of clinician instructions
card.fires_on: The first word of an instruction to the clinician, often an imperative verb such as inquire, educate, initiate or assess. It usually follows a lead-in like "Before using X," or "Prior to use,".

modes.description: Imperative verb right after a "Before/Prior to" phrase, such as inquire or assess.

modes.label: Start of a directive verb
modes.description: The opening or middle piece of a directive verb that tells the clinician to do something, such as educate, initiate or emphasize.

card.writes: It pushes toward Chinese second-person address like "for you", "you can" and "please", which suggests addressing the reader directly with advice.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label tells the clinician what to do, such as ask, assess or educate.
